title: Reply to Comment on “Deep Learning Identification of the Governing Equation for Water Flow in Heterogeneous Soils From Data” by Lee et al.
content:
Abstract

We appreciate Lee et al.’s interest in our article on identifying governing equations for water flow in heterogeneous soils. For their first concern regarding the role of deep learning in equation discovery, we clarify the synergy between sparse regression and deep learning. Sparse regression identifies the equation structure, while deep learning provides fine-grained estimates of the nonlinear coefficient functions that depend on water content and depth. For their second concern regarding regularization sensitivity, we explain why their alternative ridge formulation is not equivalent to the complete grouped identification procedure of Extended-DeepGS. Ridge regularization is integral to this solver: it stabilizes coefficient estimates when columns of the candidate library are correlated. Additional analyses show that the method consistently recovers the reference equation structure as the ridge parameter varies by nearly three orders of magnitude. More broadly, we hope this exchange promotes transparent and interpretable approaches to data-driven equation discovery in hydrology.
